items.title: Malaysians in Jakarta advised to remain calm following earthquake
items.summary: JAKARTA: Malaysians residing in or visiting Jakarta and its surrounding areas are advised to stay calm and keep up-to-date with official information issued by local authorities, following a magnitude 6.5 earthquake that struck near the capital's Thousand Islands (Kepulauan Seribu) early Saturday morning. "Overseas-bound Malaysians are advised to plan their journeys accordingly, including by allocating extra funds for personal needs, in addition to getting adequately insured prior to departure," the embassy said. For consular assistance, Malaysians may contact the Embassy of Malaysia in Jakarta at its fixed line +62 21 522 4947 or WhatsApp or call +62 813 8081 3036.

items.title: Kelantan Umno leader says sorry to Pas for 'three villains' remark
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Kelantan Umno delegate Datuk Zawawi Othman has apologised to Pas for referring to some of its leaders as the 'three villains'. "Pas, I apologise. Let us do this together," he said while debating the Umno president's policy speech at the 2026 Umno general assembly.

items.title: Malaysia, Ethiopia to hold first bilateral talks in KL next year
items.summary: NEW DELHI: Malaysia and Ethiopia will convene their first bilateral consultation in Kuala Lumpur next year as both countries seek to build on growing diplomatic momentum following reciprocal visits by their leaders. The meeting also highlighted the strengthening of bilateral relations following Abiy's visit to Malaysia in 2024 and Anwar's visit to Ethiopia in 2025. Anwar expressed appreciation for Ethiopia's support for Malaysia's engagement with BRICS, as Malaysia seeks to use the grouping to expand economic and diplomatic ties with emerging markets.

items.title: Anwar calls for 'maximum restraint' as Middle East conflict drags on
items.summary: NEW DELHI: Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has called on all parties to exercise "maximum restraint" amid the continued conflict in the Middle East. During a bilateral meeting with Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian on the sidelines of the 18th BRICS Leaders' Summit, Anwar expressed Malaysia's "deep concern" over the conflict and escalating tensions across the region. Anwar also welcomed the longstanding diplomatic relations between Malaysia and Iran and reaffirmed Malaysia's commitment to strengthening bilateral cooperation across various areas of mutual interest.

items.title: Malaysia, Ethiopia explore wider economic cooperation across key sectors
items.summary: NEW DELHI: Malaysia and Ethiopia are exploring wider economic cooperation in halal products, agriculture, food security, pharmaceuticals, digital services, renewable energy and tourism as both countries seek to turn closer diplomatic ties into commercial opportunities. The two leaders discussed opportunities to expand cooperation across sectors, with potential to boost trade, investment and private-sector participation. Malaysia's expertise in the halal economy could support cooperation with Ethiopia in halal products, certification, food processing and related industries.

items.title: Zambry meets students, stakeholders over new law replacing Auku
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Higher Education Minister Datuk Seri Dr Zambry Abdul Kadir has met student representatives as part of efforts to draft a new law to replace the Universities and University Colleges Act 1971 (Auku). Zambry said he had also begun discussions with various groups, including academics, university administrators and other stakeholders, to ensure their views were taken into account in formulating the new legislation. Zambry said student groups were also being consulted, including student representative councils.

items.title: Malaysia's strategic location draws local, global drug syndicates
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia's proximity to the "Golden Triangle" spanning Thailand, Myanmar and Laos has led drug cartels to use the country as a transit hub for the distribution of illicit drugs. Bukit Aman Narcotics Crime Investigation Department (NCID) director Datuk Hussein Omar Khan said that apart from Malaysia's strategic location, local and international syndicates were also exploiting social visit passes to enter the country and carry out illegal activities. He said these factors made Malaysia attractive to criminals as a hub or transit country for drug trafficking and smuggling activities by land, air and sea.

items.title: Malaysia, Iran seek broader trade and investment ties
items.summary: NEW DELHI: Malaysia and Iran are seeking to broaden trade and investment ties across energy, agriculture, food security, palm oil, the halal economy, technology and higher education. At their bilateral meeting, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim and Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian discussed expanding existing commercial ties. Major exports included palm oil, while imports from Iran included oil and gas products.

items.title: Ramanan: Anwar's Tamil Nadu engagement dropped due to scheduling
items.summary: NEW DELHI: Human Resources Minister Datuk Seri R. Ramanan has urged parties to stop politicising and sensationalising the decision not to proceed with a planned engagement in Tamil Nadu during Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim's India visit. Ramanan said the change to Anwar's itinerary was due to scheduling constraints, with the Prime Minister's programme already packed with high-level bilateral meetings, business engagements and his participation in the 18th BRICS Leaders' Summit. He was responding to speculation in Malaysian and Indian media over a potential meeting between Anwar and Tamil Nadu Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay during the prime minister's visit to India.

items.title: Justice delayed must still be justice delivered — Syed Mohammed Idid
items.summary: Justice must be done — and done well. Justice may take time. Institutions may change.

items.title: Police nab 2 men, seizes drugs after 50km chase in Kota Tinggi
items.summary: JOHOR BARU: Police arrested two men after a 50km high-speed chase involving members of the mobile patrol vehicle unit of the Crime Prevention and Community Safety Department, Kota Tinggi district police headquarters early today. Kota Tinggi police chief superintendent Yusof Othman said the incident occurred at about 12.35am when policemen ordered a Proton Wira to stop at Jalan Tun Sri Lanang, Bandar Kota Tinggi. He said the suspects also tested positive for methamphetamine.

items.title: Blue Malaysia Agenda to be included in BN GE16 manifesto, says Zambry
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Umno's Blue Malaysia Agenda will be incorporated into Barisan Nasional's manifesto for the 16th General Election (GE16), said Datuk Seri Dr Zambry Abdul Kadir. The BN secretary-general said the agenda, outlined by Umno president Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi in his policy speech at the 2026 Umno General Assembly, would be translated into the coalition's election manifesto. Zahid had said that the agenda would be pursued if Umno, BN, and their political allies return to power in Putrajaya.

items.title: After Bandar Tasik Selatan PPR gets RM350,000 makeover, MP asks residents to ‘take good care’ for sake of kids and grandkids
items.summary: Bandar Tun Razak Member of Parliament Datuk Seri Dr Wan Azizah Wan Ismail said repair works on the lifts at the apartments would also be carried out soon to ensure residents’ comfort. We must work together to develop and maintain them so that our children and grandchildren can also enjoy the benefits,” she said while officiating the Bandar Tun Razak Parliamentary Constituency Kenduri Rakyat Madani 2026 programme here today. Dr Wan Azizah said the initiative demonstrated how collaboration among the community, management bodies and the private sector could deliver better facilities for residents.

items.title: Ministry monitoring haze impact on Malaysian students in Indonesia
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The Higher Education Ministry is monitoring the prolonged haze in Indonesia to ensure the safety of thousands of Malaysian students studying there, says Datuk Seri Dr Zambry Abdul Kadir. The higher education minister said officials from Education Malaysia Global Services (EMGS), a company under the ministry, were tracking air quality across key regions, including Sumatra, Java and Sulawesi. Indonesia has been experiencing prolonged haze, with several regions recording deteriorating air quality.

items.title: Parliament Open Day platform to bring democratic institution closer to people - Speaker
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The Malaysia Parliament Open Day 2026, being held today and tomorrow, serves as a platform to bring the institution closer to the people, while providing the public with an opportunity to see and understand the functions and processes taking place in the 'house of democracy'. Dewan Rakyat Speaker Tan Sri Dr Johari Abdul said the public's interest in understanding the role of the institution could be seen among visitors who arrived as early as 7.30am, including visitors from abroad. "People can come and see, not only the Parliament building but also what goes on inside Parliament.

items.title: ‘We still have until February 2028’, Pakatan sec-gen says as GE16 chatter grows
items.summary: PEKAN, Sept 12 — Pakatan Harapan secretary-general Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail today brushed aside calls for the 16th general election to be held earlier, saying the Madani government’s term only expires in February 2028. Saifuddin Nasution was responding to questions from reporters after officiating the launch of the 2026 Madani Adopted Village and School by the Immigration Department at Sekolah Kebangsaan Nenasi here, national news agency Bernama reported. Anwar is from the same party and coalition as Saifuddin Nasution.

items.title: Sarawak govt leaves heli crash probe to CAAM, says state minister
items.summary: MIRI: The Sarawak government is leaving the investigation into the Flying Doctor Service (FDS) helicopter crash near Long Lellang, Ulu Baram, to the Civil Aviation Authority of Malaysia (CAAM). Sarawak Transport Minister Datuk Seri Lee Kim Shin said the state government had obtained information on the flight operation upon receiving news of the crash. He said the state government was still awaiting approval from Malaysia Airports and CAAM to resume flight operations at Long Lellang Airport.

items.title: Umno Youth seeks role in drafting BN manifesto for GE16
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Umno Youth wants a direct role in preparing the Barisan Nasional (BN) manifesto for the 16th General Election (GE16), particularly on issues affecting younger Malaysians. Negri Sembilan Umno Youth chief Mohamad Fadil Md Zain said the voices of young Malaysians must be reflected in the BN manifesto after various issues affecting the people were raised during the assembly. "President, we have discussed various issues concerning young people.

items.title: Were the 30 Malaysians caught in Indonesia lone scammers, or something bigger? Home Ministry to dig deeper
items.summary: PEKAN, Sept 12 — Malaysia will conduct an investigation following the detention of 30 Malaysians suspected of being involved in online scam activities in Pontianak, West Kalimantan, Indonesia. Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail said the country’s authorities would take appropriate action regarding the matter. Meanwhile, Saifuddin Nasution, who is also Pakatan Harapan secretary-general, said the Madani Government’s focus was currently on prioritising issues affecting the people.

items.title: Foreign Ministry seeks DNA samples of Nepal flood victims to identify missing Malaysians
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 12 — Malaysia is reportedly in talks with Nepal to have DNA samples from flood victims found during search-and-rescue operations sent here for matching against samples taken from relatives of Malaysians who remain missing, Foreign Minister Datuk Seri Mohamad Hasan said today. According to Utusan Malaysia , Mohamad said the initiative was proposed because Nepalese authorities face shortages of facilities and equipment needed to identify victims. Mohamad reportedly said Malaysia was also considering sending DNA experts to Nepal, while the Malaysian Embassy in Kathmandu has asked Nepalese security authorities to forward samples already collected from recovered victims.

items.title: Captain Zainol Afiq's remains expected to be buried in Senawang tomorrow
items.summary: SEREMBAN: The remains of Flying Doctor Service (FDS) helicopter crash victim Captain Zainol Afiq Bee Sham are expected to be buried in Senawang tomorrow. His father, Bee Sham Ahmad, 59, said the family was currently waiting for the deoxyribonucleic acid (DNA) test results after samples were taken when they arrived in Miri on Wednesday. He said the remains would be taken directly to Masjid Bandar Baru Senawang, Senawang, before being buried at Forest Height Muslim cemetery, Senawang.

items.title: Mission done, but not over: Smart team on way home as Nepal search continues
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 12 — The Special Malaysia Disaster Assistance and Rescue Team (Smart), which participated in the Humanitarian Assistance and Disaster Relief mission in Nepal, is expected to return home today or tomorrow, said Foreign Minister Datuk Seri Mohamad Hasan. “The Smart team leader will provide a report and assess the next steps so that we do not make hasty decisions; if they (Nepal) require assistance from Malaysia, we can consider helping with the search or rescue operations,” he said. The Smart MAS01 team, participating in the Humanitarian Assistance and Disaster Relief mission to Nepal, arrived in the country via Tribhuvan International Airport, Kathmandu, on September 5.

items.title: [UPDATED] Assets of second pilot linked to arrested Malaysia Airlines pilot frozen
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Police have frozen bank accounts and financial assets linked to a second pilot arrested over the seizure of RM45 million worth of drugs from a Malaysia Airlines pilot in Indonesia in July. Narcotics Crime Investigation Department (NCID) director Datuk Hussein Omar Khan said the second pilot, who is suspected of acting as a go-between for the Malaysia Airlines pilot and a drug syndicate, will be held for 60 days under the Dangerous Drugs (Special Preventive Measures) Act. Hussein added that investigators are now scrutinising the pilot's bank accounts and other financial records linked to him.

items.title: Anwar to Iran: Keep Hormuz open, choose diplomacy over conflict
items.summary: NEW DELHI, Sept 12 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim expressed concern over the continued conflict and escalation across West Asia during a bilateral meeting with Iran President Masoud Pezeshkian today. “Malaysia urged all parties to return to dialogue and diplomacy to resolve disputes and de-escalate the situation,” the prime minister said during a 30-minute meeting between the two leaders on the sidelines of the summit here. Anwar, who is also finance minister, welcomed Putrajaya and Tehran’s long-standing diplomatic relations and reaffirmed cooperation on various fronts.

items.title: Malaysia to investigate 30 citizens detained in Indonesia over online scams
items.summary: PEKAN: Malaysia will conduct an investigation following the detention of 30 Malaysians suspected of being involved in online scam activities in Pontianak, West Kalimantan, Indonesia. Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail said the country's authorities would take appropriate action regarding the matter. https://www.nst.com.my/news/nation/2026/09/1530752/30-malaysians-arrested-indonesia-over-alleged-online-scam-syndicate Meanwhile, Saufiddin Nasution, who is aso Pakatan Harapan secretary-general, said the Madani government's focus was currently on prioritising issues affecting the people.

items.title: First bodies of Philippines ferry fire victims land as toll hits 35
items.summary: PHILIPPINES: The bodies of passengers killed in a ferry fire off the Philippines arrived at a port near the resort town of Coron, Palawan on Saturday morning, as the country's coast guard warned the death toll of 35 would grow. Coast guard spokeswoman Noemie Cayabyab told a Saturday press conference the remains would be turned over to police forensic investigators for "proper disposition and identification" before allowing local authorities to inform family members. Asked how many bodies remained aboard the ship, she said authorities would provide an update later in the day.

items.title: GE16 should be held early as government has entered 'election period', says Asyraf
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Umno believes the 16th General Election (GE16) should be brought forward as the current government's term has entered what it calls the "election period". Umno secretary-general Datuk Seri Asyraf Wajdi Dusuki said the "election period" referred to the period after three years of a government's administration, when an election could be held although Parliament's maximum five-year term had not yet ended. "The election period means any time after three years is a period in which an election can be held," he said after visiting the media centre for the 2026 Umno General Assembly.

items.title: Umno won’t ‘betray anyone’ or seek new PM before next general election, says Asyraf Wajdi
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 12 — Umno secretary-general Datuk Seri Asyraf Wajdi Dusuki today said the party would not seek to change the prime minister or form a new government before the next general election is called. He said Umno remained committed to political stability and had yet to begin negotiations for the next general election. Speculation over Umno strengthening political ties with PAS intensified after PAS secretary-general Datuk Seri Takiyuddin Hassan and several other senior party leaders attended the Umno General Assembly yesterday.

items.title: Too early to say if BN will continue with PH after GE16, says Asyraf
items.summary: He said formal negotiations had yet to begin and would only be held after Parliament was dissolved. As the president said, wait until Parliament is dissolved. He said Umno's position on future political cooperation would depend on the outcome of negotiations and the political landscape at the time.

items.title: 4,646 domestic violence cases recorded from January to July
items.summary: JOHOR BARU: A total of 4,646 domestic violence cases were recorded nationwide from January to July this year, said Deputy Women, Family and Community Development Minister Lim Hui Ying. Lim said this situation served as an important reminder that prevention efforts, early intervention and access to assistance channels must be continuously strengthened through initiatives by the Women's Development Department. She said Johor recorded 823 cases, compared with 518 cases reported during the same period in 2025.

items.title: Umno wants federal administration referred to as unity government
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Umno wants the current administration to continue being referred to as the Malaysia Unity Government instead of Malaysia Madani, its secretary-general Datuk Dr Asyraf Wajdi Dusuki said. But when the Malaysia Madani Government is highlighted instead of the Malaysia Unity Government as agreed, that is the first issue. Asyraf said the agreement involved 18 parties, meaning the administration was not a government belonging to a single political party.

items.title: Three cars buried under rubble as fence wall collapses in Seremban
items.summary: SEREMBAN: A homeowner was jolted awake by a loud, thunder-like sound early this morning, only to discover that a fence wall under construction had collapsed and damaged three cars. It turned out that the side section of my fence wall, which was still under construction, had completely collapsed and fallen onto three cars belonging to my neighbours parked outside. He also said he would rebuild the wall.

items.title: Mother's home-cooked meal left untouched after son dies in Johor crash
items.summary: The victim's mother, Samsiah Kassan, 67, said she had prepared 'sambal ayam' for her youngest son, Mohamad Shahrul Azizi Sa'adon, 29, to take to work. The accident occurred yesterday at 7.30am, near the factory where the victim worked. Samsiah said her youngest of four children had eaten the breakfast she prepared before leaving home for work as usual.

items.title: Stop hunting for jobs, start creating them, minister tells TVET grads as 97pc find work
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Sept 12 — The Ministry of Youth and Sports (KBS) provides avenues and opportunities for graduates with disabilities, including those with autism, to enter the workforce, including the public service, after completing their studies at the Youth and Sports Skills Training Institutes (ILKBS). Its Minister, Dr Mohammed Taufiq Johari, said the ministry maintained data on ILKBS graduates and alumni each year to track their career paths, with most securing opportunities in the industry, as well as in the private and public sectors. Mohammed Taufiq said 4,155 graduates received their certificates at this year’s convocation after completing diploma, advanced certificate and skills certificate programmes in various fields offered by ILKBS, including 130 youths with disabilities and autism.

items.title: Umno sets up committee to explore cooperation with Pas
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Umno will form a negotiation committee to handle possible political cooperation with Pas, as calls grow within the party for closer ties with the Islamist party. Umno secretary-general Datuk Dr Asyraf Wajdi Dusuki said the committee would be established by the party leadership following views expressed by delegates at the 2026 Umno general assembly. Asyraf said Umno had previously held negotiations with both Pas and Perikatan Nasional (PN) during past elections.

items.title: Modi calls for removal of 10 key BRICS trade barriers
items.summary: NEW DELHI: Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi has urged BRICS member countries to remove 10 major trade barriers as India seeks to position itself as a bridge between the bloc and the global economy. Speaking at the BRICS Business Forum, Modi called on the BRICS Business Council to prepare a report outlining ways to eliminate the 10 key trade barriers as the 11-nation bloc of emerging economies enters its 20th year. "Can we support 100 BRICS startups each year to expand into other BRICS markets?

items.title: PH ready to contest all Melaka state seats if necessary, says Adam Adli
items.summary: MELAKA: Pakatan Harapan is ready to contest all 28 seats in the upcoming Melaka election if necessary. Previously, Melaka Chief Minister Datuk Seri Ab Rauf Yusoh said BN would only begin negotiations after the dissolution of the Melaka State Assembly, which he hinted would happen soon. Adam Adli said Melaka PH wanted the upcoming polls to be a healthy contest and not a source of division.

items.title: Empty posts, crumbling clinics: Sarawak wants the power to fix its own healthcare
items.summary: KUCHING, Sept 12 — Sarawak is pushing for regulatory powers under the Private Healthcare Facilities and Services Act 1998 (Act 586) to be decentralised to the state Health Department (JKNS), said Deputy Premier Datuk Amar Dr Sim Kui Hian. Dr Sim also called for urgent action to address Sarawak’s shortage of health personnel, with 5,654 vacant posts currently under JKNS. Dr Sim said health was among the more complex MA63 matters, involving 41 laws.

items.title: Police still hunting robbers behind RM2.9mil Jalan Ampang condo heist
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Police are still hunting for the armed robbers who broke into a condominium unit on Jalan Ampang on Monday and made off with RM2.9 million in cash and valuables. Wangsa Maju police chief Assistant Commissioner Annas Sulaiman said there were no new developments at the moment. The victim lodged a police report the same evening.

items.title: Common for parties to seek general election after three years, says Tok Mat
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: It is common for political parties to seek a fresh mandate from voters after a government had been in power for three years, Umno deputy president Datuk Seri Mohamad Hasan said. "Political parties will always want to seek a fresh mandate from the people," he said. Mohamad said Umno, as one of the political parties with a stake in the country's political landscape, also wanted to secure a fresh mandate from its supporters and voters.

items.title: Early morning blaze guts first floor of Kuching retail chain, no injuries reported
items.summary: KUCHING, Sept 12 — A fire broke out at a retail chain near Jalan Tun Ahmad Zaidi Adruce here early on Saturday morning. The Sarawak Fire and Rescue Department (better known locally as Bomba) dispatched firefighters from the Batu Lintang fire station after receiving a call at around 3.42am. “The fire broke out on the first floor involving various goods.

items.title: Lawyer denies govt forfeited funds in Abdul Azeez family’s Tabung Haji accounts
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 12 — A lawyer for former Tabung Haji (TH) chairman Datuk Seri Abdul Azeez Abdul Rahim has reportedly denied claims that the government forfeited RM18 million held in TH accounts belonging to his family members. Instead, Amer reportedly said the charge read out at the Sessions Court on September 8 alleged that Azeez used his position as TH chairman to obtain the chairmanship of Putrajaya Perdana Bhd, which brought benefits including annual remuneration, a vehicle and a permanent driver. Amer also reportedly said the Royal Commission of Inquiry into TH had made no finding that Azeez had taken or misappropriated TH funds for himself or his family, adding that Azeez has pleaded not guilty to the charge.

items.title: Economy minister says Malaysia to deepen renewable energy, connectivity ties with Indonesia, Thailand
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 12 — Malaysia is committed to strengthening regional cooperation in the field of renewable energy and connectivity as an effort to expand economic opportunities at the sub-regional level of Asean, said Minister of Economy Akmal Nasrullah Mohd Nasir. He said that sub-regional approaches such as the Indonesia-Malaysia-Thailand Growth Triangle (IMT-GT) can strengthen the economic potential among member countries through the implementation of more structured and effective plans. FDI inflows increased from US$27.52 billion (RM112.1 billion) to US$28.44 billion (RM115.9 billion), while the unemployment rate declined from 3.8 per cent to 3.7 per cent, reflecting the subregion’s economic resilience.

items.title: Sarawak dialysis patient’s rescue shows why the Flying Doctor Service matters
items.summary: KUCHING, Sept 12 — When a helicopter crashed just 200 metres from her home in Long Lellang, Renai Iwat was not only confronted with the trauma of losing a vital link to medical care, but also another race against time. Renai was eventually airlifted from Long Lellang to Miri Hospital on Thursday (Sept 10) by a Bomba helicopter, allowing her to resume the treatment on which she depends. Renai Iwat seated aboard the Bomba helicopter en route to Miri Hospital, accompanied by rescue personnel after her successful medical evacuation from Long Lellang.

items.title: No special treatment in Peter Anthony’s release, says Prisons Department
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 12 — Malaysia’s Prisons Department said the release of former Sabah Infrastructure Minister Datuk Peter Anthony under the Licensed Prisoner Release Programme (PBSL) was granted after he met the required eligibility period and underwent the same screening and assessment process as other prisoners considered for the programme. However, serving this minimum period does not automatically qualify a prisoner for release under PBSL,” it added. “Regarding the release of former Sabah Infrastructure Minister Datuk Peter Anthony, the Prisons Department stresses that consideration for his participation in PBSL was made after he reached the prescribed eligibility period and underwent the screening and assessment process applied to other candidates considered for the programme,” it said.

items.title: DNA results of Long Lellang crash victims finally in, families set to receive remains
items.summary: MIRI, Sept 12 — The DNA (deoxyribonucleic acid) test results for the five victims of the Flying Doctor Service (FDS) helicopter crash in Long Lellang in Baram have been obtained, and the remains will be handed over to the next of kin today, said Sarawak Police Commissioner Datuk Mohamad Zainal Abdullah. Meanwhile, funeral arrangements are under way for three of the five victims, as their families prepare to bid their final farewells. Medical assistant Alexson Adit Henry will be laid to rest at the Anglican Cemetery in Lambir following a funeral service at the Good Shepherd Church in Lutong at 9 am on Sept 15.

items.title: Jalan Syed Putra-Jalan Istana intersection to close in stages from Sept 14
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 12 — A section of Jalan Syed Putra and Jalan Istana intersection here will be closed in stages starting September 14, from 10pm to 5am, to facilitate preliminary construction work for the New Pantai Expressway Extension Project (NPE 2). New Pantai Expressway Sdn Bhd (NPE) announced in a statement today that the partial road closures and the implementation of temporary traffic management measures would be carried out in accordance with the construction schedule. NPE also reminded road users to adhere to safety guidelines and exercise increased caution when passing through the construction area.

items.title: Police arrest Sabah man on suspicion of murdering mother in Tambunan
items.summary: KOTA KINABALU, Sept 12 — Police arrested a 31-year-old man on suspicion of murdering his mother at a rented house in Kampung Katagayan, Tambunan, yesterday. Keningau district police chief Supt Erwansyah Abdul Basir said police were alerted to the incident involving the 56-year-old victim at about 2pm and subsequently tracked down the suspect. “The suspect was taken to the Tambunan police station, where he was arrested by the Criminal Investigation Department team from the Keningau district police headquarters,” he said in a statement today.

items.title: One-kilometre stretch of NSE lane closed near Ipoh as landslide precaution
items.summary: IPOH, Sept 12 — The left lane of the North-South Expressway near a landslide at Kilometre 263.6 southbound will be closed along a one-kilometre stretch as a safety precaution, police said today. Perak police chief Datuk Mohd Alwi Zainal Abidin said the closure would extend from Kilometre 262.8 to Kilometre 263.8, with safety cones placed along the route. He said no contraflow lane had been activated and traffic conditions were being continuously monitored.

items.title: PM Anwar, Putin agree to establish mechanism to fast-track Malaysia-Russia deals
items.summary: NEW DELHI, Sept 12 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim, in a bilateral meeting with Russian President Vladimir Putin, has suggested the establishment of a special mechanism between Putrajaya and Moscow to expedite the execution of all agreements reached between the two nations. Both leaders also discussed about the import of Malaysian palm oil by Moscow and expediting direct flights between both countries during their meeting, held on the sidelines of the 18th Brics Leaders’ Summit here on yesterday. Meanwhile, Russian news agency TASS quoted Putin as describing the 12.9 per cent growth in trade turnover between Russia and Malaysia last year as “a solid pace.”

items.title: ‘Slayyy’: PM Anwar turns ‘Guru’ for Malaysia’s Brics diplomatic mission
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 12 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim hopes Malaysia’s diplomatic mission at the 18th Brics Leaders’ Summit in India will achieve its objectives, while his light-hearted reference to himself as “Guru” in a Facebook post after arriving in New Delhi caught the attention of netizens. Anwar said he was bringing Malaysia’s voice to the prestigious global platform, guided by the Madani Diplomacy framework. “Alhamdulillah, Guru has safely arrived in New Delhi, India to represent the country on the world stage at the 18th Brics Leaders’ Summit.

items.title: King renews Putin’s invitation to visit Malaysia through PM Anwar at Brics summit
items.summary: NEW DELHI, Sept 12 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim conveyed warm regards from His Majesty Sultan Ibrahim, King of Malaysia to Russian President Vladimir Putin during their bilateral meeting here yesterday. “Sultan Ibrahim sends his personal regards,” Anwar said. The Prime Minister also reiterated Sultan Ibrahim’s invitation to Putin to make a state visit to Malaysia.

items.title: New school curriculum to introduce Sabah identity elements in Year One and Form One next year
items.summary: KOTA KINABALU, Sept 12 — Elements reflecting Sabah’s identity will be incorporated into the new school curriculum for Year One and Form One students from the next academic session, Education Minister Datuk Seri Fadhlina Sidek said. Fadhlina said Sabah Education, Science, Technology and Innovation Minister Datuk James Ratib had given his full support to the proposal. Fadhlina said incorporating elements of Sabah’s identity into the curriculum was important in strengthening ties among Sabah, Sarawak and Peninsular Malaysia, which she described as a foundation of Malaysia’s strength.

items.title: Malaysia-Russia ties in focus as PM Anwar, Putin meet at Brics summit
items.summary: It marked Anwar’s first bilateral meeting upon his arrival here to participate in the summit in Malaysia’s capacity as a BRICS partner country since January 1, 2025. The meeting underscored the importance of maintaining high-level engagement between the two countries, particularly as Malaysia seeks to deepen economic and strategic ties with major emerging economies. Malaysia and Russia have maintained longstanding diplomatic relations since 1967, with cooperation spanning trade and investment, energy, education, tourism, defence and other areas.

items.title: Anwar welcomes Western push to ban trade with illegal Israeli settlements
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 12 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has welcomed the joint statement issued on September 8 by the foreign ministers of 12 Western countries regarding measures against illegal Israeli settlements. He said the steps represent an overdue shift in the approach of several Western governments and must now be matched by firm implementation. Anwar said he noted in particular that Britain, Canada and France would bring forward measures to ban trade in settlement goods, joining several European countries that have already taken this step.

items.title: MCMC probes claims Claude AI targeted Malaysian voters, but says issue outside its mandate
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Sept 11 — The Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission (MCMC) is examining claims that Anthropic’s Claude artificial intelligence platform was used to operate a commercial election manipulation campaign targeting users in Malaysia. MCMC said it took the US AI company’s latest report seriously but stressed that the activities described fell outside its functions and mandate. “MCMC was not involved in any activities or dealings as described in the report,” it said in a statement today.

items.title: Anwar to meet Modi, leading Indian companies on Brics summit sidelines today
items.summary: NEW DELHI, Sept 12 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim is scheduled to have three bilateral meetings today on the sidelines of the 18th Brics Leaders’ Summit here. His third bilateral meeting is with Ethiopian Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed. India assumed its fourth BRICS chairship on January 1, 2026.

items.title: KL DOE warns of fake procurement scams after two suppliers lose more than RM200,000
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 11 — The Kuala Lumpur Department of Environment (DOE) has detected several attempts by irresponsible parties to commit fraud using the department’s name. She said her department first detected the scam on September 4, when a representative of a diving equipment supplier came to the department to verify the authenticity of government procurement documents. “Prior to that, KL DOE also received several inquiries regarding these government procurement documents starting in mid-August, and last Tuesday (September 8) from a supplier company representative who also came to inquire about a souvenir order worth more than RM100,000 supposedly made by KL DOE for an upcoming programme,” she told Bernama, here today.

items.title: Fire Dept: Two men found dead in separate incidents in Penang drain and Perak river
items.summary: BUTTERWORTH, Sept 11 — Two men were found dead in separate incidents in Penang and Perak today, one in a drain near a school here and the other in Sungai Perak. The body of Ooi Chai Siang, 37, was found in a drain about 1.5 metres deep near Sekolah Menengah Kebangsaan (SMK) Tun Hussein Onn in Taman Kelisa Emas here today. Penang Fire and Rescue Department (JBPM) Operations assistant director John Sagun Francis said the department received a call from the police at 12.10pm requesting assistance to retrieve the body.

items.title: PM Anwar heads to India for BRICS summit, bilateral talks with world leaders
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 11 — After concluding his working visit to Sabah today, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim departed for New Delhi to attend the 18th BRICS Leaders’ Summit, where he is also scheduled to hold several bilateral meetings. In a Facebook post, Anwar said he was scheduled to meet the Prime Minister of India, as well as the presidents of Russia, Iran and Kazakhstan and the Prime Minister of Ethiopia. “My delegation and I have departed for New Delhi, India to attend the 18th BRICS Leaders’ Summit.
